breakpoint_attempt.observed: CS=4465 EIP=00000000 was never seen in any poll. The debugger console repeatedly showed '(Running)' or stale text from the earlier 411B breakpoint hit. The polling loop exited only because the Ollama agent hit its own max-steps=100 and exited, which the outer while loop treats as a stop condition.

root_cause_hypothesis.claim_boundary: hypothesis only, not proven this session -- offered to focus the next attempt
root_cause_hypothesis.text: The CPU was confirmed running (not stopped) when 'BPDEL *' and 'BP 4465:0000' were typed, unlike every earlier successful BP arm in this same run (parser/tactical), which were all typed while the debugger was confirmed stopped at a prior breakpoint. WriteConsoleInput-based command injection should still be picked up by DOSBox-X's debugger on its next input-check cycle regardless of run state, but this run's evidence is consistent with the command being registered too late, being dropped, or being consumed by the running DOS session instead of the debugger. No direct BPLIST readback was taken immediately after arming to confirm registration -- that is the cheapest next diagnostic.

suggested_next_attempt: Add an immediate 'BPLIST' + snapshot right after 'BP 4465:0000' is sent (before RUN) to confirm registration independent of whether the breakpoint later fires.
Consider tightening the poll interval for this specific watch (currently 2s) to rule out a hit-and-silently-resumed race, though the '(Running)' scrollback argues against this.
Consider arming the breakpoint earlier, while the CPU is still confirmed stopped from the load-monster/tactical checkpoint, rather than after the F5/free-run.

If BPLIST confirms registration but it still never fires, escalate to BPM on the physical write address (0x44BB1) as an alternative trigger, accepting the known DOSBox-X BPM segment-alias caveat already documented for the area-word watch.
